candidates.title: Saudi Falcons Club Auction
candidates.summary: The Saudi Falcons Club organizes an annual auction dedicated to locally caught falcons, known as “Al Tarh falcons,” which are captured during the hunting season. The auction is a structured platform that brings falconers together to showcase their falcons in a competitive live bidding environment, enabling reliable buying and selling. The event is broadcast on television channels and digital platforms. The club also provides integrated services for falcon owners, including transportation to the auction venue, along with facilities that organize and enhance the participation experience, all within a framework aimed at developing falcon auctions in Saudi. The auction also contributes to raising awareness about preserving falcon breeds by regulating sales and emphasizing the protection of endangered species.

candidates.rich_summary: The Jameel Library presents ‘At the Edge of Renewal’, a six-month exhibition developed by the Khaleeji Women’s Library & Archive (KWLA) and curated by Jood AlThukair , including work from Nouf AlHarthi , Hayfa AlGwaiz , Abeer Sultan , Dalal AlObaidi , Yasmeen Abdal , Fatima Al Jarman and Maitha Ali , among others. ‘At the Edge of Renewal’ is part of a series of exhibitions at the Jameel Library that invites book artists, librarians and publishers to reimagine the library through curated displays and reading lists. Each iteration becomes a library within the library, offering new ways to encounter collections, ideas and practices of reading. Taking Ursula K. Le Guin’s 1981 essay “World-Making” as its point of entry, the exhibition begins with the idea of a world already here, already made, and the work of remaking it from within.

candidates.title: Riyadh Racing Season
candidates.summary: Experience the excitement of the Riyadh Racing Season 2026–2027 at King Abdulaziz Racecourse, running from October 16, 2026, to April 17, 2027. The season features 50 race days, with races held on Fridays and Saturdays throughout the season. The season brings together some of the most prestigious local and international horse races and cups, including the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Cup, the Crown Prince Cup, and the Kings' Cups, alongside major races featuring leading horses and jockeys. Saudi Cup 2027 is the highlight of the season, taking place on February 5–6, 2027, with ⃁ 75 million in prize money, making it the world's richest horse race. It is followed by the Founder King Abdulaziz Cup on March 12, 2027, featuring the King Abdulaziz Arabian Horses Cup and the King Abdulaziz Locally Bred Horses Cup, with ⃁ 5 million in prize money. Across 24 weeks, race nights combine thrilling competitions with hospitality and dining experiences, alongside entertainment, cultural activities, and family-friendly experiences.

candidates.title: Palms Village in Al Ahsa
candidates.summary: Discover Palms Village, a sustainable rural destination set among the palm farms of Al Ahsa, home to one of the world's largest palm oases. The village brings together the local heritage, authentic flavors, and traditions that make the region unique. Stroll through shops offering Saudi dates and date products, sample local dishes at restaurants and cafés, and shop for rural products from Al Ahsa. Enjoy traditional performances and discover local crafts, including bisht weaving and khoos, the art of weaving palm fronds. Explore the history of palm trees and their importance to the region at the Palm Museum, and spend quality time with family in dedicated family areas and children's activities. The village welcomes visitors daily from 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM until February 28, 2027.

candidates.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra
candidates.summary: Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. It is within these confines that the echoes of laughter from childhood games intermingle with the remnants of disagreements and tears shed upon pillows. The scent of maternal cooking and the rhythmic snoring of a father create a comforting ambiance, while the presence of a grandmother before the television grounds us in familial continuity. These shared experiences resonate universally, forging a collective nostalgia for "al zaman al Jameel

candidates.title: Tafasahu: Make Room
candidates.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra
candidates.summary: Tafasahu: Make Room is an exhibition that showcases a commissioned installation by Saudi architect and artist, Nada AlMulla, which invites you to enter as a guest—to pause, gather and reflect on the conditions of belonging within the context of the traditional Majlis, Arabic for "gathering space." Beyond being a place to receive and host guests, the Majlis has been a vessel for the transmission of knowledge and heritage. The installation deconstructs this space into its essential elements while centering stories, memories and subtle traces of everyday life that animated it: conversations shared over coffee, the lingering scent of incense, the rhythms of gathering and departure. Hospita

candidates.image_alt: Hayy Arts | Made With Your Magic - Jeddah
candidates.rich_summary: The exhibition borrows its Arabic title, ‘Suni‘a Bisihrika’, from a phrase created to facilitate the memorization of the eight main Eastern (Arabic) musical maqâms. Each letter in this phrase represents the first letter of a main maqâm’s name. They are formal musical structures that have been used for centuries across a vast geography extending from the Arab world to neighboring regions and Central Asia. Beyond their function as aesthetic musical structures, maqâms carry layered historical, cultural, social and political meanings shaped over centuries. Looking closely at their names, genealogies and circulation reveals that they reflect a rich artistic and cultural diversity beyond national, religious, and linguistic identity. They point instead to long histories of exchange, coexistence, translation, movement and rupture. They have endured through political shifts, cycles of exclusion and persecution, wars and the collapse of empires.

candidates.title: Arabic Calligraphy × Woodworks: From Script to Object
candidates.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra
candidates.summary: This workshop explores the transformation of Arabic calligraphy from a written system into a constructed wooden object. Participants engage with letterforms as structural elements rather than decorative motifs, translating them into physical compositions through a process that combines sketching, digital vectorization and fabrication. Course Objectives: Understand the structural logic of Arabic calligraphy beyond visual aesthetics Explore the relationship between language and material Develop the ability to translate two dimensional script into physical objects Learn the fundamentals of vector design for fabrication Gain awareness of wood properties and fabrication constraints Course Outcome

candidates.title: AlUla Tour
candidates.organizer: Royal Commission for AlUla / Experience AlUla
candidates.summary: AlUla Tour is a major fixture on the international cycling calendar, attracting the world’s top teams and riders for a multi-stage race through one of the most spectacular landscapes on Earth. From dramatic desert backdrops to iconic landmarks like Maraya and the Oasis, each stage delivers high performance and unforgettable scenery in equal measure. Individual AlUla Tour stages will be announced closer to the race date, but previous editions have seen riders traverse routes from Old Town to Harrat Uwayrid and Winter Park to Wirkah Mountain.

candidates.title: Human Capability Initiative Conference
candidates.venue: King Abdulaziz International Conference Center (KAICC), Riyadh
candidates.summary: Under the patronage of His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince, Prime Minister, and Chairman of the Human Capability Development Program (HCDP) Committee, the third edition of the Human Capability Initiative (HCI) Conference—one of the Saudi Vision 2030 Realization Programs—will take place on April 12–13, 2027, at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme “The Human Code.” The conference will focus on three pillars: deep human connection, sound reasoning amid complexity, and value-driven creation to safeguard human contribution and purpose in the age of accelerated technological advancement. HCI 2027 aims to attract more than 15,000 visitors and over 250 local and international speakers, including policymakers, thought leaders, and experts from government, private, nonprofit, and global institutions, providing a platform to exchange best practices and showcase inspiring global success stories. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland will participate as Country of Honor, reflecting the strength of the Saudi-British strategic partnership in advancing human capability development. Building on the success of previous editions—which welcomed over 23,000 visitors, featured 550+ speakers, and announced more than 156 launches and agreements—the conference reinforces the Kingdom’s commitment to investing in human potential as a foundation for sustainable growth and global competitiveness in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030.
